## Update LLVM version mappings for ghc-8.6 compilers

The GHC 8.6 series of compilers (8.6.1 through 8.6.5) officially require LLVM 6 for their LLVM backend, but the current configuration in `overlays/bootstrap.nix` incorrectly specifies LLVM 5 for these versions. This causes warning messages about a version mismatch whenever the LLVM backend is used — for example, during cross-compilation workflows.

The goal is to align the LLVM package versions used by these compilers with the officially supported requirements. Specifically:

- The `buildLlvmPackages` and `llvmPackages` attributes for all ghc-8.6.X entries (ghc861, ghc862, ghc863, ghc864, ghc865) in `overlays/bootstrap.nix` need to be updated from LLVM 5 to LLVM 6.
- Note: ghc-8.4.4 (also in this file) correctly uses LLVM 5 and should not be changed. GHC 8.8.1 requires LLVM 7, but haskell.nix does not currently support ghc-8.8.1, so no changes are needed for that version.
- A changelog entry should be added documenting this fix.

To verify the change, try building a Haskell package that uses the LLVM backend with one of the ghc-8.6.X compilers and check that the LLVM version warning no longer appears.

## Environment Setup
Check `overlays/bootstrap.nix` for the compiler configuration to modify, and `changelog.md` for documentation. For build and test instructions, review `default.nix`, `shell.nix`, and `test.nix`.

## Implementation Plan
- Locate the ghc861 through ghc865 definitions in `overlays/bootstrap.nix`
    - Replace references to `llvmPackages_5`/`buildLlvmPackages_5` with the corresponding LLVM 6 variants (e.g., `llvmPackages_6`/`buildLlvmPackages_6`) for each ghc-8.6 entry
    - Leave the ghc844 entry unchanged since LLVM 5 is correct for GHC 8.4.4
    - Add a dated summary entry to `changelog.md` describing the fix
    - Verify no other references to LLVM 5 exist that should also be updated for consistency

1: This file contains a summary of changes to Haskell.nix and `nix-tools`
2: that will impact users.
3: 
4: ## November 18, 2019
5:   * Changed the `cleanSourceHaskell` to accept an attrset of `src` and
6:     (optional) `name` parameters. This allows you to keep the source
7:     derivation name constant, so that your builds are always
8:     cached. Usage of `cleanSourceHaskell` will need to be updated.
9: 
10: ## October 12, 2019
11:  * [`shellFor`](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/library/#shellfor) no longer sets `CABAL_CONFIG` by default.
12:    This avoids surprising users, but means that Cabal may select a plan which is different to your Haskell.nix package set.
13:    If you would like the old behaviour, use `shellFor { exactDeps = true; }`.
14: 
15: ## August 9, 2019
16:  * Add the [`haskellLib.collectComponents`](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/library/#haskellLib) function.
17:

    The problem is that downstream consumers often need the bare executable name (e.g., `package-name` or `package-name.exe` on Windows) rather than the path with the `bin/` prefix. Providing the bare name is more useful and flexible — it allows consumers to construct paths however they need (e.g., `${drv}/bin/${drv.exeName}`) and is easier to work with in various Nix expressions.

    2. Update the consumers of this attribute accordingly.

9: 
10: =haskell.nix= is an experimental new builder for Haskell packages.
11: 
12: It works by automatically translating your Cabal or Stack project and
13: its dependencies into Nix code.  It provides IFD (imports from derviation)
14: functions that can minimize the amount of nix code you need to add.
15: 
16: For the documentation, see https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/.
17: 
18: ** Quickstart
19: 
20: For =cabal.project= project add a =default.nix=:
21: 
22: #+begin_src sh
23: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> (import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz))
24: , haskellCompiler ? "ghc865"
25: }:
26:   pkgs.haskell-nix.cabalProject {
27:     src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; };
28:     ghc = pkgs.buildPackages.pkgs.haskell-nix.compiler.${haskellCompiler};
29:   }
30: #+end_src
31: 
32: Note that you'll need to add a comment specifying the expected sha256
33: output for your =source-repository-packages= in your =cabal.project=
34: file:
35: 
36: #+begin_src sh
37: source-repository-package
38:   type: git
39:   location: https://github.com/input-output-hk/iohk-monitoring-framework
40:   subdir:   plugins/backend-editor
41:   tag: 4956b32f039579a0e7e4fd10793f65b4c77d9044
42:   --sha256: 03lyb2m4i6p7rpjqarnhsx21nx48fwk6rzsrx15k6274a4bv0pix
43: #+end_src
44: 
45: For a =stack.yaml= project add a =default.nix=:
46: 
47: #+begin_src sh
48: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> (import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz))
49: }:
50:   pkgs.haskell-nix.stackProject {
51:     src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; };
52:   }
53: #+end_src
54: 
55: To build the library component of a package in the project run:
56: 
57: #+begin_src sh
58: nix build -f . your-package-name.components.library
59: #+end_src
60: 
61: To build an executable:
62: 
63: #+begin_src sh

66: 
67: To open a shell for use with `cabal` run:

1: This file contains a summary of changes to Haskell.nix and `nix-tools`
2: that will impact users.
3: 
4: ## December 27, 2019
5:   * Fixed the LLVM version used by the GHC 8.6 series of compilers
6:     (ghc861 through ghc865). They now use LLVM 6 as officially
7:     required, instead of LLVM 5, eliminating version mismatch warnings
8:     when the LLVM backend is used (e.g. in cross-compilation workflows).
9: 
10: ## November 18, 2019
11:   * Changed the `cleanSourceHaskell` to accept an attrset of `src` and
12:     (optional) `name` parameters. This allows you to keep the source
13:     derivation name constant, so that your builds are always
14:     cached. Usage of `cleanSourceHaskell` will need to be updated.
15: 
16: ## October 12, 2019
17:  * [`shellFor`](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/library/#shellfor) no longer sets `CABAL_CONFIG` by default.
18:    This avoids surprising users, but means that Cabal may select a plan which is different to your Haskell.nix package set.
19:    If you would like the old behaviour, use `shellFor { exactDeps = true; }`.
20: 
21: ## August 9, 2019
22:  * Add the [`haskellLib.collectComponents`](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/library/#haskellLib) function.
23: 
24: ## June 21, 2019
25:  * Add `ghcWithPackages` and `ghcWithHoogle` to hsPkgs ([documentation](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/library/#package-set-functions).
26:  * Benchmark components can now build successfully.
27:  * Reduced the closure bloat of nix-tools, and added closure size limit to CI.
28:  * Added more reference documentation and set up auto-generated
29:    documentation for [Module Options](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/reference/modules/).
30:  * Miscellaneous bug fixes.
31: 
32: ## June 7, 2019
33:   * Several additions to the [documentation](https://input-output-hk.github.io/haskell.nix/).
34:     * More information about getting nix-tools, Haskell.nix, pinning.
35:     * Updates the stack-to-nix and cabal-to-nix guides.
36:     * Adds a section on development environments.
37:     * Adds a little information about cross compilation.
38:     * Adds a (partially complete) reference section (command line manuals, library reference).
39:     * Symlinks the changelog into the documentation pages.
40: 
41: ## May 29, 2019
42:   * Added `shellFor` function to package set.
43: 
44: ## May 28, 2019
45:   * Added `snaphots` and `haskellPackages` attributes to the
46:     Haskell.nix top-level.
47: 
48: ## May 22, 2019
49:   * Add the `cleanSourceHaskell` utility function to the Haskell.nix
50:     top-level.
51: 
52: ## May 21, 2019
53:   * Add the `callCabalProjectToNix` function, which uses "import from
54:     derivation" (IFD) so that nix-tools doesn't need to be run
55:     manually.
56:   * The `hackage.nix` update process has changed, so that Cabal index
57:     state hashes are also included in the generated repo.
58: 
59: ## May 20, 2019
60:   * Remove Travis CI in favour of Buildkite.
61: 
62: ## May 17, 2019
63:   * Add the `callStackToNix` function, which uses "import from
64:     derivation" (IFD) so that `stack-to-nix` doesn't need to be run
65:     manually.
66: 
67: ## Mar 15, 2019
68:   * `overlays` was renamed to `extras` in

70:     to prevent confusion between the notion of Nix overlays.

<type>file</type>
<content>
1: # This is a source filter function which cleans common build products
2: # and files not needed to do a haskell build from a source directory.
3: #
4: # This can avoid unecessary builds when these files change.
5: #
6: # It should be used with "pkgs.lib.cleanSourceWith". Alternatively,
7: # use the convenience function "cleanSourceHaskell".
8: #
9: { lib }:
10: 
11: rec {
12:   haskellSourceFilter = name: type:
13:     let baseName = baseNameOf (toString name);
14:     in ! (
15:       # Filter out cabal build products.
16:       baseName == "dist" || baseName == "dist-newstyle" ||
17:       baseName == "cabal.project.local" ||
18:       lib.hasPrefix ".ghc.environment" baseName ||
19:       # Filter out stack build products.
20:       lib.hasPrefix ".stack-work" baseName ||
21:       # Filter out files left by ghci
22:       lib.hasSuffix ".hi" baseName ||
23:       # Filter out files generated by "hasktags"
24:       baseName == "TAGS" || baseName == "tags" ||
25:       # Filter out files which are commonly edited but don't
26:       # affect the cabal build.
27:       lib.hasSuffix ".nix" baseName
28:     );
29: 
30:   # Like pkgs.lib.cleanSource, but adds Haskell files to the filter.
31:   cleanSourceHaskell = { src, name ? null }:
32:     let
33:       clean = lib.cleanSourceWith {
34:         filter = haskellSourceFilter;
35:         src = lib.cleanSource src;
36:         inherit name;
37:       };
38:       # Copy function from 19.09 for compatibility with 19.03.
39:       # Does require at least Nix 2.0.
40:       compat = let
41:         isFiltered = src ? _isLibCleanSourceWith;
42:         origSrc = if isFiltered then src.origSrc else src;
43:         filter' = name: type: haskellSourceFilter name type && lib.cleanSourceFilter name type;
44:         name' = if name != null then name else if isFiltered then src.name else baseNameOf src;
45:       in {
46:         inherit origSrc;
47:         filter = filter';
48:         outPath = builtins.path { filter = filter'; path = origSrc; name = name'; };
49:         _isLibCleanSourceWith = true;
50:         name = name';
51:       };
52:     in
53:       if (builtins.typeOf src) == "path"
54:       then (if lib.versionAtLeast lib.version "19.09" then clean else compat) else src;
55: }

<content>
1: Cross compilation of Haskell projects involves building a version of
2: GHC that outputs code for the target platform, and providing builds of
3: all library dependencies for that platform.
4: 
5: First, understand how to cross-compile a normal package from
6: Nixpkgs. Matthew Bauer's [Beginners' guide to cross compilation in
7: Nixpkgs][bauer] is a useful resource.
8: 
9: [bauer]: https://matthewbauer.us/blog/beginners-guide-to-cross.html
10: 
11: 
12: Using an example from the guide, this builds GNU Hello for a Raspberry
13: Pi:
14: 
15:     nix build -f '<nixpkgs>' pkgsCross.raspberryPi.hello
16: 
17: We will use the same principle in [Haskell.nix][] — replacing the normal
18: package set `pkgs` with a cross-compiling package set
19: `pkgsCross.raspberryPi`.
20: 
21: ### Raspberry Pi example
22: 
23: This is an example of using [Haskell.nix][] to build the [Bench][]
24: command-line utility, which is a Haskell program.
25: 
26: ```nix
27: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {} }:
28: let
29:   haskellNix = import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz);
30:   native = haskellNix { inherit pkgs; };
31: in
32:   native.haskellPackages.bench.components.exes.bench
33: ```
34: 
35: Now switch the package set as in the previous example:
36: 
37: ```nix
38: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {} }:
39: let
40:   haskellNix = import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz);
41:   raspberryPi = haskellNix { pkgs = pkgs.pkgsCross.raspberryPi; };
42: in
43:   raspberryPi.haskellPackages.bench.components.exes.bench
44: ```
45: 
46: You should be prepared for a long wait because it first needs to build
47: GHC, before building all the Haskell dependencies of [Bench][]. If all
48: of these dependencies compiled successfully, I would be very surprised!
49: 
50: !!! hint
51:     The above example won't build, but you can try and see, if you like.
52:     It will fail on [clock-0.7.2](http://hackage.haskell.org/package/clock-0.7.2),
53:     which needs a patch to build.
54: 
55: To fix the build problems, you must add extra configuration to the
56: package set. Your project will have a [`mkStackPkgSet`](../reference/library.md#mkstackpkgset) or
57: [`mkCabalProjectPkgSet`](../reference/library.md#mkcabalprojectpkgset). It is there where you must add
58: [module options](../reference/modules.md) for setting compiler flags, adding patches, and so on.
59: 
60: 
61: ### Static executables with Musl libc
62: 
63: Another application of cross-compiling is to produce fully static
64: binaries for Linux. For information about how to do that with the
65: [Nixpkgs Haskell infrastructure][nixpkgs] (not [Haskell.nix][]), see
66: [nh2/static‑haskell‑nix][nh2]. Vaibhav Sagar's linked
67: [blog post][vaibhav] is also very informative.
68: 
69: 
70: ```nix
71: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {} }:
72: let
73:   haskellNix = import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz);
74:   musl64 = haskellNix { pkgs = pkgs.pkgsCross.musl64; };
75: in
76:   musl64.haskellPackages.bench.components.exes.bench
77: ```
78: 
79: This example will build [Bench][] linked against Musl libc. However
80: the executable will still be dynamically linked. To get fully static
81: executables you must add package overrides to:
82: 
83: 1. Disable dynamic linking
84: 2. Provide static versions of system libraries. (For more details, see
85:    [Vaibhav's article][vaibhav]).
86: 
87: ```nix
88: {
89:   packages.bench.components.exes.bench.configureFlags =
90:     stdenv.lib.optionals stdenv.hostPlatform.isMusl [
91:       "--disable-executable-dynamic"
92:       "--disable-shared"
93:       "--ghc-option=-optl=-pthread"
94:       "--ghc-option=-optl=-static"
95:       "--ghc-option=-optl=-L${gmp6.override { withStatic = true; }}/lib"
96:       "--ghc-option=-optl=-L${zlib.static}/lib"
97:     ];
98: }
99: ```
100: 
101: !!! note "Licensing"
102:     Note that if copyleft licensing your program is a problem for you,
103:     then you need to statically link with `integer-simple` rather than
104:     `integer-gmp`. However, at present, [Haskell.nix][] does not provide
105:     an option for this.
106: 
107: 
108: ### How to cross-compile your project
109: 
110: Set up your project Haskell package set.
111: 
112: ```nix
113: # default.nix
114: { pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {}
115: let
116:   # Import the Haskell.nix library,
117:   haskell = import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz) {
118:     inherit pkgs;
119:   };
120: 
121:   # Instantiate a package set using the generated file.
122:   pkgSet = haskell.mkCabalProjectPkgSet {
123:     plan-pkgs = import ./pkgs.nix;
124:     pkg-def-extras = [];
125:     modules = [
126:       {
127:         # You will need to put build fixes here.
128:       }
129:     ];
130:   };
131: in
132:   pkgSet.config.hsPkgs
133: ```
134: 
135: Apply that package set to the Nixpkgs cross package sets that you are
136: interested in.
137: 
138: We are going to expand the `pkgs.pkgsCross` shortcut to be more
139: explicit.
140: 
141: ```nix
142: let
143:   pkgs = import <nixpkgs> {}
144: in {
145:   shortcut = pkgs.pkgsCross.SYSTEM;
146:   actual = import <nixpkgs> { crossSystem = pkgs.lib.systems.examples.SYSTEM; };
147: }
148: ```
149: 
150: In the above example, for any `SYSTEM`, `shortcut` and `actual` are
151: the same package set.
152: 
153: ```nix
154: # release.nix
155: let
156:   myProject = import ./default.nix;
157: 
158:   pkgsNative = import <nixpkgs> {};
159:   pkgsRaspberryPi = import <nixpkgs> {
160:     crossSystem = pkgsNative.lib.systems.examples.raspberryPi;
161:   };
162: 
163:   native = myProject { pkgs = pkgsNative; };
164:   crossRaspberryPi = myProject { pkgs = pkgsRaspberryPi; };
165: 
166: in {
167:   my-project-native = native.my-project.components.exes.my-project;
168:   my-project-raspberry-pi = crossRaspberryPi.my-project.components.exes.my-project;
169: }
170: ```
171: 
172: Try to build it, and apply fixes to the `modules` list, until there
173: are no errors left.
174: 
175: 
176: 
177: [nh2]: https://github.com/nh2/static-haskell-nix
178: [vaibhav]: https://vaibhavsagar.com/blog/2018/01/03/static-haskell-nix/
179: [haskell.nix]: https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix
180: [bench]: https://hackage.haskell.org/package/bench
181: [nixpkgs]: https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/#users-guide-to-the-haskell-infrastructure

1: # This is a replacement for the cleanSourceWith function in nixpkgs
2: # https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/1d9d31a0eb8e8358830528538a391df52f6a075a/lib/sources.nix#L41
3: # It adds a subDir argument in a way that allows descending into a subdirectory
4: # to compose with cleaning the source with a filter.
5: { lib }: rec {
6:   cleanSourceWith = { filter ? path: type: true, src, subDir ? "" }:
7:     let
8:       subDir' = if subDir == "" then "" else "/" + subDir;
9:       # In case this is mixed with older versions of cleanSourceWith
10:       isFiltered = src ? _isLibCleanSourceWith;
11:       isFilteredEx = src ? _isLibCleanSourceWithEx;
12:       origSrc = if isFiltered || isFilteredEx then src.origSrc else src;
13:       origSubDir = if isFilteredEx then src.origSubDir + subDir' else subDir';
14:       origSrcSubDir = toString origSrc + origSubDir;
15:       parentFilter = if isFiltered || isFilteredEx
16:         then path: type: src.filter path type
17:         else path: type: true;
18:       filter' = path: type:
19:         # Include parent paths based on the parent filter
20:            (lib.strings.hasPrefix (path + "/") (origSrcSubDir + "/")
21:             && parentFilter path type)
22:         # Children only if both filters return true
23:         || (lib.strings.hasPrefix (origSrcSubDir + "/") path
24:             && (filter path type && parentFilter path type));
25:     in {
26:       inherit origSrc origSubDir origSrcSubDir;
27:       filter = filter';
28:       outPath = (builtins.filterSource filter' origSrc) + origSubDir;
29:       _isLibCleanSourceWithEx = true;
30:       # It is only safe for older cleanSourceWith to filter this one
31:       # if the we are still looking at the root of origSrc
32:       _isLibCleanSourceWith = origSubDir == "";
33:     };

35:   pathHasContext = builtins.hasContext or (lib.hasPrefix builtins.storeDir);

38:        src ? _isLibCleanSourceWithEx

When using `cleanGit` on a repository that has submodules which themselves contain submodules, the nested submodule contents are currently excluded from the resulting filtered source tree. This happens because the filtering logic in `lib/clean-git.nix` doesn't account for the `.git` file that Git creates in a submodule directory when it has its own nested submodules — this `.git` file points to the relative location of the submodule's git metadata in the parent repository's `.git/modules` directory.

    The goal is to ensure that when `cleanGit` processes a repository with nested submodules, the `.git` file in the intermediate submodule directories is preserved. Without this file, Git cannot resolve the submodule's metadata location, so `git ls-files --recurse-submodules` fails to list the nested submodule's contents, and they get excluded from the clean source output.

1: # cleanGit
2: 
3: To filter out just the files in your git index use
4: `haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; }` where `./.` is the
5: root of your git repo (or a git work tree).
6: 
7: First it filters just the files needed to run `git index`, then
8: it uses the results of that to filter your directory.  It does not
9: need to parse the `.gitignore` files at all, but we do need to
10: `git add` our files before they will be included.
11: [cleanGit source](https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/blob/master/lib/clean-git.nix).
12: 
13: In addition haskell.nix (including `cleanGit`) uses a version
14: of [`cleanSourceWith`](https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/blob/master/lib/clean-source-with.nix)
15: with a `subdir` argument to filter out just the package it is
16: building.  Then it uses the info from the `cabal` file to filter
17: just the source dirs for the component it is building.  That way
18: if we modify a test in a package nix will not rebuild the library
19: in that package (or anything that depends on that package's library).
20: 
21: There is a downside to this though.  If we have a test that depends
22: on something outside the scope of what is described in its entry in
23: the in the `.cabal` file it will not see it.  For instance perhaps
24: it needs to run `hlint` or `doctest` on the library source.  There
25: are ways to fix this with a module:
26: 
27: Use `extraSrcFiles` to add dirs the test needs (this will not result
28: in a change to the `.cabal` file the test will still be built the same).
29: ```
30: components.tests.test.extraSrcFiles = [ "subdir-needed-by-test" ];
31: ```
32: Or alternatively, override the source with a suitable filter function. 
33: ```
34: components.tests.test.src = haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanSourceWith {
35:     inherit src;
36:     subdir = "path-to-package";
37:     filter = ...
38: };
39: ```

1: # cleanGit
2: 
3: To filter out just the files in your git index use
4: `haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; }` where `./.` is the
5: root of your git repo (or a git work tree).
6: 
7: First it filters just the files needed to run `git index`, then
8: it uses the results of that to filter your directory.  It does not
9: need to parse the `.gitignore` files at all, but we do need to
10: `git add` our files before they will be included.
11: [cleanGit source](https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/blob/master/lib/clean-git.nix).
12: 
13: In addition haskell.nix (including `cleanGit`) uses a version
14: of [`cleanSourceWith`](https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/blob/master/lib/clean-source-with.nix)
15: with a `subdir` argument to filter out just the package it is
16: building.  Then it uses the info from the `cabal` file to filter
17: just the source dirs for the component it is building.  That way
18: if we modify a test in a package nix will not rebuild the library
19: in that package (or anything that depends on that package's library).
20: 
21: There is a downside to this though.  If we have a test that depends
22: on something outside the scope of what is described in its entry in
23: the in the `.cabal` file it will not see it.  For instance perhaps
24: it needs to run `hlint` or `doctest` on the library source.  There
25: are ways to fix this with a module:
26: 
27: Use `extraSrcFiles` to add dirs the test needs (this will not result
28: in a change to the `.cabal` file the test will still be built the same).
29: ```
30: components.tests.test.extraSrcFiles = [ "subdir-needed-by-test" ];
31: ```
32: Or alternatively, override the source with a suitable filter function. 
33: ```
34: components.tests.test.src = haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanSourceWith {
35:     inherit src;
36:     subdir = "path-to-package";
37:     filter = ...
38: };
39: ```
40:

1: Here we will look into how to generate the `pkgs.nix` file for a
2: `stack.yaml` project. For the full integration see the
3: [previous page](./projects.md).
4: 
5: ## Using `stack-to-nix`
6: 
7: With [nix-tools installed](../user-guide.md), we can simply run the
8: following command on a stack project:
9: 
10: ```bash
11: stack-to-nix --output . --stack-yaml stack.yaml
12: ```
13: 
14: This will produce a `pkgs.nix` file that looks like the following:
15: ```nix
16: {
17:   resolver = "lts-12.17";
18:   extras = hackage:
19:     {
20:       packages = {
21:         "o-clock" = hackage.o-clock."0.1.1".revisions.default;
22:         ...
23:       } // {
24:         my-package = ./my-package.nix;
25:         ...
26:       };
27:     };
28: }
29: ```
30: 
31: This file contains the stackage resolver, as well as set of extra
32: packages.  The extras specifies which `extra-deps` (here:
33: `o-clock-0.1.1`) we wanted to add over the stackage snapshot, and what
34: local packages we want (here: `my-package`).
35: 
36: ## Creating the package set
37: 
38: Import the generated `pkgs.nix` and pass to
39: [`mkStackPkgSet`](../reference/library.md#mkstackpkgset) to
40: instantiate a package set.
41: 
42: ```nix
43: # default.nix
44: let
45:   # Import the Haskell.nix library,
46:   src = builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz;
47:   nixpkgs = import (src + "/nixpkgs") (import src);
48:   haskell = nixpkgs.haskell-nix;
49: 
50:   # Instantiate a package set using the generated file.
51:   pkgSet = haskell.mkStackPkgSet {
52:     stack-pkgs = import ./pkgs.nix;
53:     pkg-def-overlays = [];
54:     modules = [];
55:   };
56: in
57:   pkgSet.config.hsPkgs
58: ```

1: Here we will look into how to generate the `pkgs.nix` file for a
2: `cabal.project` project. For the full integration see the [previous
3: page](./projects.md).
4: 
5: Generating package sets for Cabal projects, is slightly more involved,
6: because you need to let Cabal calculate a build plan for the
7: dependencies of your package(s).
8: 
9: ## Generating `plan.json`
10: 
11: To get a plan, you need Cabal and GHC. See the [How to install a
12: compiler section of the Nixpkgs Manual][compiler] for information
13: about how to choose a specific compiler version.
14: 
15: [compiler]: https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/#how-to-install-a-compiler
16: 
17: !!! note "Cabal version"
18:     The minimum Cabal version is 2.4. This version is available
19:     in the NixOS 19.03 release.
20: 
21: For this example, we will run a `nix-shell` with the default GHC
22: version for Nixpkgs.
23: 
24: ```bash
25: nix-shell -p haskellPackages.cabal-install haskellPackages.ghc \
26:     --run "cabal new-configure"
27: ```
28: 
29: If all goes well, you should now have the file
30: `dist-newstyle/cache/plan.json`.
31: 
32: !!! tip "Specifying the GHC version"
33:     To use a specific compiler version, replace `haskellPackages.ghc`
34:     with something like `haskell-nix.compiler.ghc865`. The given compiler
35:     must exist in your Nixpkgs version, of course. See also the
36:     [Nixpkgs Manual][compiler].
37: 
38: ## Using `plan-to-nix`
39: 
40: With [nix-tools installed](../user-guide.md), we can then run the
41: following command on a Cabal project and its build plan. Omit the
42: `--cabal-project` option if you don't have a project file.
43: 
44: ```bash
45: # convert the plan.json file into a pkgs.nix file
46: plan-to-nix --output . \
47:     --plan-json dist-newstyle/cache/plan.json
48:     --cabal-project cabal.project
49: ```
50: 
51: This will produce a `pkgs.nix` file that looks like the following:
52: 
53: ```nix
54: {
55:   pkgs = hackage:
56:     {
57:       packages = {
58:         "o-clock" = hackage.o-clock."0.1.1".revisions.default;
59:         ...
60:       };
61:       compiler = { ... };
62:     };
63: 
64:   extras = hackage:
65:     { packages = { my-package = ./.plan.nix/my-package.nix; }; };
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: It has converted Cabal's build plan into a Nix expression that selects
70: dependencies from `hackage.nix`. All local packages in the project are
71: generated with `cabal-to-nix` and added to the package set
72: description.
73: 
74: ## Creating the package set
75: 
76: Import the generated `pkgs.nix` and pass to
77: [`mkCabalPkgSet`](../reference/library.md#mkcabalprojectpkgset) to
78: instantiate a package set.
79: 
80: ```nix
81: # default.nix
82: let
83:   # Import the Haskell.nix library,
84:   src = builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz;
85:   nixpkgs = import (src + "/nixpkgs") (import src);
86:   haskell = nixpkgs.haskell-nix;
87: 
88:   # Instantiate a package set using the generated file.
89:   pkgSet = haskell.mkCabalProjectPkgSet {
90:     plan-pkgs = import ./pkgs.nix;
91:     pkg-def-extras = [];
92:     modules = [];
93:   };
94: in
95:   pkgSet.config.hsPkgs
96: ```

1: # This is a replacement for the cleanSourceWith function in nixpkgs
2: # https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/1d9d31a0eb8e8358830528538a391df52f6a075a/lib/sources.nix#L41
3: # It adds a subDir argument in a way that allows descending into a subdirectory
4: # to compose with cleaning the source with a filter.
5: { lib }: rec {
6:   cleanSourceWith = { filter ? path: type: true, src, subDir ? "" }:
7:     let
8:       subDir' = if subDir == "" then "" else "/" + subDir;
9:       # In case this is mixed with older versions of cleanSourceWith
10:       isFiltered = src ? _isLibCleanSourceWith;
11:       isFilteredEx = src ? _isLibCleanSourceWithEx;
12:       origSrc = if isFiltered || isFilteredEx then src.origSrc else src;
13:       origSubDir = if isFilteredEx then src.origSubDir + subDir' else subDir';
14:       origSrcSubDir = toString origSrc + origSubDir;
15:       parentFilter = if isFiltered || isFilteredEx
16:         then path: type: src.filter path type
17:         else path: type: true;
18:       filter' = path: type:
19:         # Include parent paths based on the parent filter
20:            (lib.strings.hasPrefix (path + "/") (origSrcSubDir + "/")
21:             && parentFilter path type)
22:         # Children only if both filters return true
23:         || (lib.strings.hasPrefix (origSrcSubDir + "/") path
24:             && (filter path type && parentFilter path type));
25:     in {
26:       inherit origSrc origSubDir origSrcSubDir;
27:       filter = filter';
28:       outPath = (builtins.filterSource filter' origSrc) + origSubDir;
29:       _isLibCleanSourceWithEx = true;
30:       # It is only safe for older cleanSourceWith to filter this one
31:       # if the we are still looking at the root of origSrc
32:       _isLibCleanSourceWith = origSubDir == "";
33:     };
34: 
35:   pathHasContext = builtins.hasContext or (lib.hasPrefix builtins.storeDir);
36: 
37:   canCleanSource = src:
38:        src ? _isLibCleanSourceWithEx
39:     || src ? _isLibCleanSourceWith
40:     || !(pathHasContext (toString src));
41: }

<path>/code/docs/reference/library.md</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: [Haskell.nix][] contains a library of functions for creating buildable
2: package sets from their Nix expression descriptions. The library is
3: what you get when importing [Haskell.nix][]. It might be helpful to
4: load the library in the [Nix REPL](../user-guide.md#using-nix-repl) to
5: test things.
6: 
7:  * [Types](#types) — the kinds of data that you will encounter working with [Haskell.nix][].
8:  * [Top-level attributes](#top-level-attributes) — Functions and derivations defined in the Haskell.nix attrset.
9:  * [Package-set functions](#package-set-functions) — Helper functions defined on the `hsPkgs` package set.
10: 
11: # Types
12: 
13: ## Package Set
14: 
15: The result of `mkPkgSet`. This is an application of the NixOS module
16: system.
17: 
18: ```
19: {
20:   options = { ... };
21:   config = {
22:     hsPkgs = { ... };
23:     packages = { ... };
24:     compiler = {
25:       version = "X.Y.Z";
26:       nix-name = "ghcXYZ";
27:       packages = { ... };
28:     };
29:   };
30: }
31: ```
32: 
33: | Attribute      | Type | Description                                         |
34: |----------------|------|-----------------------------------------------------|
35: | `options` | Module options | The combination of all options set through the `modules` argument passed to `mkPkgsSet`. |
36: | `config` |  | The result of evaluating and applying the `options` with [Haskell.nix][] |
37: | `.hsPkgs` | Attrset of [Haskell Packages](#haskell-package) | Buildable packages, created from `packages` |
38: | `.packages` | Attrset of [Haskell Package descriptions](#haskell-package-descriptions) | Configuration for each package in `hsPkgs` |
39: | `.compiler` | Attrset | |
40: 
41: 
42: 
43: ## Haskell Package description
44: 
45: The _Haskell package descriptions_ are values of the
46: `pkgSet.config.packages` attrset. These are not derivations, but just
47: the configuration for building an individual package. The
48: configuration options are described under `packages.<name>` in [Module
49: options](./modules.md).
50: 
51: ## Component description
52: 
53: The _component descriptions_ are values of the
54: `pkgSet.config.packages.<package>.components` attrset. These are not
55: derivations, but just the configuration for building an individual
56: component. The configuration options are described under
57: `packages.<name>.components.*` in [Module options](./modules.md).
58: 
59: 
60: ## Haskell Package
61: 
62: In [Haskell.nix][], a _Haskell package_ is a derivation which has a
63: `components` attribute. This derivation is actually just for the
64: package `Setup.hs` script, and isn't very interesting. To actually use
65: the package, look within the components structure.
66: 
67: ```
68: components = {
69:   library = COMPONENT;
70:   exes = { NAME = COMPONENT; };
71:   tests = { NAME = COMPONENT; };
72:   benchmarks = { NAME = COMPONENT; };
73:   all = COMPONENT;
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ## Component
78: 
79: In [Haskell.nix][], a _component_ is a derivation corresponding to a
80: [Cabal component](https://www.haskell.org/cabal/users-guide/developing-packages.html)
81: of a package.
82: 
83: [Haskell.nix][] also defines a special `all` component, which is the
84: union of all components in the package.
85: 
86: ## Identifier
87: 
88: A package identifier is an attrset pair of `name` and `version`.
89: 
90: ## Extras
91: 
92: Extras allow adding more packages to the package set. These will be
93: functions taking a single parameter `hackage`. They should return an
94: attrset of package descriptions.
95: 
96: ## Modules
97: 
98: Modules are the primary method of configuring building of the package
99: set. They are either:
100: 
101: 1. an attrset containing [option declarations](./options.md), or
102: 2. a function that returns an attrset containing option declarations.
103: 
104: If using the function form of a module, the following named parameters
105: will be passed to it:
106: 
107: | Argument         | Type | Description         |
108: |------------------|------|---------------------|
109: | `haskellLib`     | attrset | The [haskellLib](#haskelllib) utility functions. |
110: | `pkgs` | | The Nixpkgs collection. |
111: | `pkgconfPkgs` | | A mapping of cabal build-depends names to Nixpkgs packages. (TODO: more information about this) |
112: | `buildModules` | | |
113: | `config` | | |
114: | `options` | | |
115: 
116: 
117: # Top-level attributes
118: 
119: ## mkStackPkgSet
120: 
121: Creates a [package set](#package-set) based on the `pkgs.nix` output
122: of `stack-to-nix`.
123: 
124: ```nix
125: mkStackPkgSet =
126:     { stack-pkgs, pkg-def-extras ? [], modules ? []}: ...
127: ```
128: 
129: | Argument         | Type | Description         |
130: |------------------|------|---------------------|
131: | `stack-pkgs`     |  | `import ./pkgs.nix` — The imported file generated by `stack‑to‑nix`. |
132: | `pkg‑def‑extras` | List of [Extras](#extras) | For overriding the package set. |
133: | `modules` | List of [Modules](#modules) | For overriding the package set. |
134: 
135: **Return value**: a [`pkgSet`](#package-set)
136: 
137: ## mkCabalProjectPkgSet
138: 
139: Creates a [package set](#package-set) based on the `pkgs.nix` output
140: of `plan-to-nix`.
141: 
142: ```nix
143: mkCabalProjectPkgSet =
144:     { plan-pkgs, pkg-def-extras ? [], modules ? []}: ...
145: ```
146: 
147: | Argument         | Type | Description         |
148: |------------------|------|---------------------|
149: | `plan-pkgs`     |  | `import ./pkgs.nix` — The imported file generated by `plan‑to‑nix`. |
150: | `pkg‑def‑extras` | List of [Extras](#extras) | For overriding the package set. |
151: | `modules` | List of [Modules](#modules) | For overriding the package set. |
152: 
153: **Return value**: a [`pkgSet`](#package-set)
154: 
155: ## mkPkgSet
156: 
157: This is the base function used by both `mkStackPkgSet` and
158: `mkCabalProjectPkgSet`.
159: 
160: **Return value**: a [`pkgSet`](#package-set)
161: 
162: ## snapshots
163: 
164: This is an attrset of `hsPkgs` packages from Stackage.
165: 
166: ## haskellPackages
167: 
168: A `hsPkgs` package set, which is one of the recent LTS Haskell
169: releases from [`snapshots`](#snapshots).
170: 
171: The chosen LTS is updated occasionally in [Haskell.nix][], though a
172: manual process.
173: 
174: ## nix-tools
175: 
176: A derivation containing the `nix-tools` [command-line tools](commands.md).
177: 
178: ## callStackToNix
179: 
180: Runs `stack-to-nix` and produces the output needed for
181: `importAndFilterProject`.
182: 
183: **Example**:
184: 
185: ```nix
186:   pkgSet = mkStackPkgSet {
187:     stack-pkgs = (importAndFilterProject (callStackToNix {
188:       src = ./.;
189:     })).pkgs;
190:     pkg-def-extras = [];
191:     modules = [];
192:   };
193: ```
194: 
195: 
196: ## callCabalProjectToNix
197: 
198: Runs `cabal new-configure` and `plan-to-nix` and produces the output
199: needed for `importAndFilterProject`.
200: 
201: **Example**:
202: 
203: ```nix
204:   pkgSet = mkCabalProjectPkgSet {
205:     plan-pkgs = (importAndFilterProject (callCabalProjectToNix {
206:       index-state = "2019-04-30T00:00:00Z";
207:       src = ./.;
208:     })).pkgs;
209: ```
210: 
211: | Argument         | Type | Description         |
212: |------------------|------|---------------------|
213: | `name`          | String | Optional name for better error messages. |
214: | `src`           | Path   | Location of the cabal project files. |
215: | `index-state`   | Timestamp | Optional hackage index-state, eg. "2019-10-10T00:00:00Z". |
216: | `index-sha256`  | Sha256 | Optional hash of the truncated hackage index-state. |
217: | `plan-sha256`   | Sha256 | Optional hash of the plan-to-nix output (makes the plan-to-nix step a fixed output derivation). |
218: | `cabalProject`  | Path   | Optional cabal project file (defaults to "${src}/cabal.project"). |
219: | `ghc`           |        | Optional ghc to use |
220: | `nix-tools`     |        | Optional nix-tools to use |
221: | `hpack`         |        | Optional hpack to use |
222: | `cabal-install` |        | Optional cabal-install to use |
223: | `configureArgs` | String | Optional extra arguments to pass to `cabal new-configure` (--enable-tests is included by default, include `--disable-tests` to override that). |
224: 
225: ## importAndFilterProject
226: 
227: Imports from a derivation created by `callStackToNix`
228: or `callCabalProjectToNix`.
229: 
230: The result is an attrset with the following values:
231: 
232: | Attribute      | Type | Description                                         |
233: |----------------|------|-----------------------------------------------------|
234: | `pkgs` | attrset | that can be passed to `mkStackPkgSet` (as `stack-pkgs`) or `mkCabalProjectPkgSet` (as `plan-pkgs`). |
235: | `nix` | | this can be built and cached so that the amount built in the evaluation phase is not too great (helps to avoid timeouts on Hydra). |
236: 
237: ## hackage
238: ## stackage
239: 
240: ## fetchExternal
241: 
242: ## cleanSourceHaskell
243: 
244: ```
245: cleanSourceHaskell = { src, name ? null }: ...
246: ```
247: 
248: Filters a source tree removing common filenames that are not Haskell
249: build sources.
250: 
251: This can avoid unecessary rebuilds when these files change.
252: 
253: It's recommended to provide `name` so that the source derivation
254: remains constant regardless of how it was fetched.
255: 
256: Example:
257: 
258: ```
259: src = pkgs.haskell-nix.cleanSourceHaskell {
260:   src = ./.;
261:   name = "myproject-src";
262: };
263: ```
264: 
265: ## haskellSourceFilter
266: 
267: ```
268: haskellSourceFilter = name: type: ...
269: ```
270: 
271: This is a source filter function which cleans common build products
272: and files not needed to do a Haskell build from a source directory.
273: 
274: It should be used with `pkgs.lib.cleanSourceWith`. Alternatively,
275: use the convenience function [`cleanSourceHaskell`](#cleansourcehaskell).
276: 
277: 
278: ## haskellLib
279: 
280: Assorted functions for operating on [Haskell.nix][] data. This is
281: distinct from `pkgs.haskell.lib` in the current Nixpkgs Haskell
282: Infrastructure.
283: 
284: ### collectComponents
285: 
286: Extracts a selection of components from a Haskell [package set](#package-set).
287: 
288: This can be used to filter out all test suites or benchmarks of
289: your project, so that they can be built in Hydra (see check if you
290: waht to run the tests as well as build them).
291: 
292: ```
293: collectComponents =
294:     group: packageSel: haskellPackages: ...
295: ```
296: 
297: 
298: | Argument          | Type   | Description         |
299: |-------------------|--------|---------------------|
300: | `group`           | String | A [sub-component type](#subComponentTypes). |
301: | `packageSel`      | A function `Package -> Bool` | A predicate to filter packages with. |
302: | `haskellPackages` | [Package set](#package-set)    | All packages in the build. |
303: 
304: **Return value**: a recursive attrset mapping package names → component names → components.
305: 
306: **Example**:
307: 
308: ```nix
309: tests = collectComponents "tests" (package: package.identifier.name == "mypackage") hsPkgs;
310: ```
311: 
312: Will result in moving derivations from `hsPkgs.mypackage.components.tests.unit-tests`
313: to `tests.mypackage.unit-tests`.
314: 
315: #### check
316: 
317: This function turns a derivation that builds a test into one to run it.
318: 
319: | Argument          | Type   | Description         |
320: |-------------------|--------|---------------------|
321: | `drv`           | Derivation | One of `$pkg.components.tests.$test`. |
322: 
323: For convenience `$pkg.components.tests` are mapped with this function
324: to `$pkg.components.checks`.
325: 
326: This function is intended for use with `tests` but it should also work
327: for `exes` and `benchmarks` if you just want to run them to make sure
328: they execute.
329: 
330: #### subComponentTypes
331: 
332: Sub-component types identify [components](#component) and are one of:
333: 
334:  - `sublibs`
335:  - `foreignlibs`
336:  - `exes`
337:  - `tests`
338:  - `benchmarks`

340: # Package-set functions
341: 
342: These functions exist within the `hsPkgs` package set.
343: 
344: ## shellFor
345: 
346: Create a `nix-shell` [development
347: environment](../user-guide/development.md) for developing one or more
348: packages with `ghci` or `cabal v2-build` (but not Stack).
349: 
350: ```
351: shellFor =
352:     { packages, withHoogle ? true, exactDeps ? false, ...}: ...
353: ```
354: 
355: 
356: | Argument       | Type | Description         |
357: |----------------|------|---------------------|
358: | `packages`     | Function | Package selection function. It takes a list of [Haskell packages](#haskell-package) and returns a subset of these packages. |
359: | `withHoogle` | Boolean | Whether to build a Hoogle documentation index and provide the `hoogle` command. |
360: | `exactDeps` | Boolean | Prevents the Cabal solver from choosing any package dependency other than what are in the package set. |

369:     [known limitation](../dev/removing-with-package-wrapper.md)
370:     which we would like to solve. Use `exactDeps = false` if this is a
371:     problem.

375: 
376: Creates a `nix-shell` [development
377: environment](../user-guide/development.md) including the given
378: packages selected from this package set.
379: 
380: **Parameter**: a package selection function.
381: 
382: **Return value**: a derivation

191: ### Pinning the [Haskell.nix][] version
192: 
193: For simplicity's sake we will use `fetchTarball` for the examples in
194: this documentation. This will always get the latest version, and is
195: similar to an auto-updating Nix channel.
196: 
197: However, in your own project, you may wish to pin [Haskell.nix][] (as
198: you would pin Nixpkgs). This will make your builds reproducable, more
199: predictable, and faster (because the fixed version is cached).
200: 
201: One way of doing this is to use `nix-prefetch-git` to get a JSON file
202: with a revision and SHA-256 hash of [Haskell.nix][].
203: 
204: ```
205: $ nix-prefetch-git --quiet https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix | tee haskell-nix-src.json
206: {
207:   "url": "https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix",
208:   "rev": "f1a94a4c82a2ab999a67c3b84269da78d89f0075",
209:   "date": "2019-06-05T01:06:12+00:00",
210:   "sha256": "0ggxsppjlb6q6a83y12cwgrdnqnw1s128rpibgzs5p1966bdfqla",
211:   "fetchSubmodules": false
212: }
213: ```
214: 
215: (The `tee` command is just to show you the result.)
216: Use the following expression to import that version:
217: 
218: ```nix
219: { nixpkgs ? <nixpkgs> }:
220: 
221: let
222:   spec = builtins.fromJSON (builtins.readFile ./haskell-nix-src.json);
223:   haskell-nix-src = (import nixpkgs {}).fetchgit {
224:     name = "haskell-lib";
225:     inherit (spec) url rev sha256 fetchSubmodules;
226:   };
227: in
228:   import nixpkgs (import haskell-nix-src)
229: ```
230: 
231: There are other possible schemes for pinning. See
232: [`haskell.nix/lib/fetch-external.nix`](https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/blob/master/lib/fetch-external.nix),
233: the [niv](https://github.com/nmattia/niv) tool, or the Nix Flakes
234: proposal.
235: 
236: ### Overriding the Hackage version
237: 
238: Sometimes you might want to use a chosen version of Haskell.nix with a
239: recent update of Hackage or Stackage. This can be done with JSON pins:
240: 
241: ```bash
242: nix-prefetch-git https://github.com/input-output-hk/hackage.nix | tee hackage-src.json
243: nix-prefetch-git https://github.com/input-output-hk/stackage.nix | tee stackage-src.json
244: ```
245: 
246: The resulting JSON files will correspond to the latest revision of
247: [hackage.nix][] and [stackage.nix][]. See
248: [Architecture](architecture.md) for more information about how
249: these Git repositories correspond to the actual Hackage and Stackage.
250: 
251: [hackage.nix]: https://github.com/input-output-hk/hackage.nix
252: [stackage.nix]: https://github.com/input-output-hk/stackage.nix
253: 
254: ```nix

256:   (self: super: {
257:     haskell-nix = super.haskell-nix // {
258:       hackageSourceJSON  = ./hackage-src.json;
259:       stackageSourceJSON = ./stackage-src.json;

3: [Haskell.nix][] can be use for two different use cases:
4: 
5: ### Use 1 : to build a specific package from hackage or a [stackage][] lts or nightly set.
6: 
7: To build a package, say [lens][], from a stackage snapshot, say [lts-13.28][],
8: you could run
9: ```bash
10: nix build '(with import <nixpkgs> (import ./.); haskell-nix.snapshots."lts-13.28").lens.components.library'
11: ```
12: which would build the [lens][] library component from the lens package as fixed
13: by the [lts-13.28][] stackage snapshot.
14:    
15: To build any package from hackage, say [lens][], in version, say 4.17.1, you
16: could run
17: ```bash
18: nix build '(with import <nixpkgs> (import ./.); (haskell-nix.hackage-package { name = "lens"; version = "4.17.1"; })).components.library'
19: ```
20: which would build the [lens][] library component from the [lens-4.17.1][] package
21: from hackage.  The dependencies would be solved against the most recent 
22: [hackage-index-state][] that comes via the [hackage.nix][] pin with your
23: [haskell.nix][] checkout.  A specific one can be specified as well:
24: ```bash

26: ```
27: which would use the hackage index as of `2019-07-14T00:00:00Z` to produce a build plan
28: for the [lens-4.17.1][] package.
29:

    The problem manifests when working with git worktrees where `.git` is a file (not a directory) containing `gitdir: <path>`. The current implementation uses `toString` on paths that may contain Nix store path interpolations, which doesn't work correctly in a sandboxed context.

The fix should handle the case where we're composing paths from Nix store paths (which may be in the Nix store) with relative paths from the `commondir` file or the `gitdir` reference.

    Please ensure the fix maintains the existing behavior for regular git repositories while properly handling worktree scenarios. The change should be minimal and focused on the path composition logic in the `commonConfig` binding.

                            if db == 0:

                    i = j
                    continue
                i += 1

        if c == "'" and i+1 < n and s[i+1] == "'":

    return db, dp, neg

+### Custom source filters
+
+When passing a project to `stackProject` or `cabalProject` you can add
+a custom filter function to the `src` argument to control which files
+are included in the build, for example to exclude parts of the
+repository that are not needed:
+
+```nix
+{ pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> (import (builtins.fetchTarball https://github.com/input-output-hk/haskell.nix/archive/master.tar.gz))
+}:
+  pkgs.haskell-nix.cabalProject {
+    src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanSourceWith {
+      src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; };
+      # Exclude the given directory and everything under it.
+      filter = path: type:
+        baseNameOf path != "static" || type != "directory";
+    };
+  }
+```
+
+Your filter function should be written in terms of the two arguments
+`path` and `type` (as for the built-in `filterSource` function).
+`cleanGit` (used as the `src` above) will only include files from the
+git index, so custom filters are most useful for selecting subdirectories
+of the repository or excluding generated files that are tracked by git.
+
+!!! warning "Avoid using filterSource here"
+    For this purpose you should use `cleanSourceWith` from `haskellLib`
+    rather than the built-in `filterSource` function (or the
+    `lib.cleanSourceWith` from Nixpkgs).  Filtering the source with
+    `filterSource` causes unnecessary rebuilds of **all** components of
+    the project whenever any part of the source changes.
+
+`haskellLib.cleanSourceWith` is a replacement for the
+`lib.cleanSourceWith` function from Nixpkgs.  In addition to the
+`filter` argument it supports a `subDir` argument, so you can filter
+the source and descend into a subdirectory of the repository in a
+single step (see also the `cleanGit` example above, where `subDir` is
+used to point at a project that is not at the root of the repo):
+
+```nix
+src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanSourceWith {
+  src = pkgs.haskell-nix.haskellLib.cleanGit { src = ./.; };
+  subDir = "path/to/project";
+  filter = path: type: ...;
+};
+```
